`scgsim.palace.EigenmodeSim` owns mutable mesh, config, resolved-port and handoff
state. It is separate from Electrostatic and AEDT, with no common simulation
base object. The [Palace lesson](../course/palace-eigenmode.qmd) teaches the
ordinary sequence; [Xmon EPR](../tutorial-xmon-palace.qmd) adds optional physics.

| Stage | Public surface |
|---|---|
| Shared source | `set_plan(GeometryPlanSnapshot)` |
| Standalone source | `set_geometry(component)` and `set_stack(stack)` on a fresh unbound simulation |
| Output | `set_output_dir(path)` |
| Eigenmode | `set_eigenmode(*, num_modes=10, target=None, tolerance=1e-6, save=0)` |
| Mesh controls | `set_mesh(...)` accepts the shared sizing recipe, mesher options, repair budgets and quality threshold |
| Mesh summary | `mesh_summary()` returns detached meshing evidence |
| Numerical controls | `set_numerical(...)` retains explicit order, linear solver, AMR and output choices |
| Source/settings view | `input_summary()` returns detached source plus settings, no file/native I/O |
| Surface model | `set_surface_epr(*, representation, specs, route_a_thin_film=None)`, before `mesh()` |
| Authored port | `add_port(qualified_name, *, layer, layout_sheet=True, inductance)` |
| Output selection | `set_epr_request(*, surface_interfaces=None, bulk_domain_ids=None, port_names=None)` |
| Preparation | `mesh()`, `write_config()`, then `prepare_handoff(*, profile, executable, resources=None, setup_commands=(), petsc_options=())` |

Geometric order is distinct from the FEM order configured through
`set_numerical(...)`; solver settings preserve the current mesh controls. The
Eigenmode and Electrostatic facades share one set of mesh controls and
defaults, described in the
[Palace mesh controls](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-controls), which
also state that a mesh below the quality threshold stops `mesh()`.

## Eigenmode mesh and AMR defaults (CONVERGING)

A fresh `EigenmodeSim` uses the shared default mesh controls
(`FeatureRecipe()`, `MesherOptions()`, `Budgets()` and a `0.01` quality
threshold) and writes `Model.Refinement.Nonconformal=true`. Before
`write_config()`, provide `amr_max_passes` through `set_numerical(...)`. For a
positive pass limit, also provide `amr_tolerance` and `amr_update_fraction`;
setting `amr_max_passes=0` disables adaptive refinement and allows those two
values to remain unset. Omitted values in later `set_numerical(...)` calls
retain their current settings. These are input controls, not adequacy
recommendations. Electrostatic retains its existing AMR defaults in the shared
contract.

`mesh_summary()` reports recorded meshing controls, native element and region
counts, and mesh identities. Its Nédélec degree-of-freedom value is a
topological estimate from primary-corner tetrahedra and the configured FEM
order, not a solver-reported DOF count. Changing FEM order refreshes that
estimate without remeshing. These mesh records do not establish numerical
adequacy.

Target frequency is in hertz, mesh lengths in micrometres, inductance in henries.
Ordinary Eigenmode does not require surface specs, ports or an EPR request.
A bound plan carries the shared envelope and cannot be partially replaced by
standalone geometry/stack or conflicting envelope setters. The
[GeometryPlan contract](../geometry-sgb.qmd) owns source identity and route
preparation. The [Electrostatic/shared Palace contract](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd)
owns the shared mesh controls and config controls.

## Selection and physical meaning

Surface selectors are `MA`, `MS`, `SA`. Bulk selectors are the SGB solution-volume
`entry_name` values from `Domains.Postprocessing.Energy`. Port selectors are
configured `LayoutPortBinding.name` values. `None` selects all configured
entries, `()` selects none, and a subset must resolve against the exact written
index. Unknown selections fail during config writing or result extraction.
Filtering output does not delete physical domains/ports or change normalization.

### Surface-film inputs and native material side

Surface-film inputs bind exact source surfaces and physical attributes to the
Palace `MA`, `MS`, or `SA` type and its film assumptions. Provide exactly one
of `thickness` (native model units) or `film_thickness_m` (converted using
`Model.L0`), and exactly one of numeric `permittivity` or `material_id` that
resolves to an explicit dielectric. `loss_tangent` may be supplied directly or
read from that material; an unknown value remains distinguishable in SCGSim's
index. The current `surface-film.v2` producer rejects missing or duplicated
surface and physical-attribute identities rather than dropping or deduplicating
them. Film thickness sets the surface model, and
[inset margins](#surface-epr-margins) set any requested exclusion near the gaps.

Palace 0.18.1 forms native surface integrands from the configured type and the
neighboring solution elements: `MA` and `SA` use the vacuum-side trace, while
`MS` uses the substrate-side trace. `MA` uses normal electric field, `MS` uses
the substrate-permittivity-weighted normal field, and `SA` combines tangential
and normal terms with the film permittivity. See Palace 0.18.1's
[configuration](https://github.com/awslabs/palace/blob/0dc74cdf8c36c58b69b21c4a06e816048ec0b83f/palace/utils/configfile.cpp#L624)
and [neighbor-material rules](https://github.com/awslabs/palace/blob/0dc74cdf8c36c58b69b21c4a06e816048ec0b83f/palace/fem/coefficient.hpp#L331)
for the native mapping. Choose `MA`, `MS`, or `SA` to match the
intended native interface model.

### Surface-EPR margins {#surface-epr-margins}

An inset margin $m$ selects the part of a surface at least $m$ µm from the
nearest gap edge, the edge of a conductor footprint that faces exposed
substrate. SGB cuts that part into the model as band faces, so stock Palace
integrates ordinary attributes; SCGSim writes no native `Mask` or `Inset`
configuration, and no special Palace build is needed. The
[SGB design pages](../../zh-TW/docs/design/sgb/inset-imprint.html#band-measure)
(Traditional Chinese) define how distance is measured.

Narrow bands need a mesh that resolves them, and outlines drawn as many short
edges make both the bands and the mesh harder to build: see
[meshing narrow bands](#surface-epr-band-meshing) and
[curved outlines](#surface-epr-curved-outlines) below.

::: {.callout-important title="Call set_surface_epr before mesh()"}
Margins are geometry: `mesh()` hands them to SGB with the rest of the model.
Configure `set_surface_epr` first. Calling it after `mesh()` invalidates the mesh,
config and handoff, and `mesh()` must run again.
:::

Each spec (`"MA"`, `"MS"`, `"SA"`) takes these margin keys next to its film
inputs:

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `inset_margins_um` | Strictly increasing positive margins in µm. `mesh()` asks SGB for bands at these margins on every face of the spec's type, in one geometry build. Omit it for baseline rows only. |
| `inset_margins_by_entity_um` | `{entity_id: [margins]}` for `MA` and `MS`. Each named conductor takes its own margins, and the rest of the type keeps `inset_margins_um`, if given. It adds one extra, unbanded geometry build to find the conductors' faces. A named conductor with no face of that type raises `ValueError` from `mesh()`. It is rejected for `SA`, whose interface lies between solution regions and has no owning conductor. |
| `face_kinds` | Restricts the spec to some of `"sheet"`, `"top"`, `"bottom"` and `"interface"`. When the spec asks for margins, `"sidewall"` is rejected because SGB never bands sidewalls. |
:::

A margin of `0` is rejected: the baseline row already covers the whole surface.

One face has one band family, so it takes one set of margins. A Route A sheet
carries both an `MA` and an `MS` row, so when both specs reach it they must give
it the same margins, compared on the model grid (`0.3` and `0.1 + 0.2` agree).
Differing margins on one sheet are an error: `mesh()` raises `ValueError`
naming the conductor, the face and both sets when it can see the conflict from
`inset_margins_by_entity_um`, and otherwise SGB refuses the build with an
`InputError` that names the two requests. Margins are never merged. Every margin
must be a positive multiple of the model grid; a customised margin off the grid
is refused by `mesh()` before any comparison.

Each surface row gets a baseline row that covers all its faces. Each margin adds a
further row covering the bands from that margin outward. Margin rows are
alternative evaluations of the same surface, not disjoint bands: read each row
separately and do not add them. SGB bands a face only where it has a gap edge, so
a face without one, such as the underside of a substrate, is covered only by the
baseline row. The manifest lists the faces SGB skipped.

Group names attach the face kind to the entity with `__`, for example
`MA::pad__top::band=1`. The [naming rule](../../zh-TW/docs/design/sgb/identity.html#band-group-names)
is owned by the SGB design pages; read band membership from the index map instead
of parsing names.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Rows, sides and cracked sheets"}
The index map (schema v3) records, for each surface row, its `row` and `group`,
`interface_type`, `band`, `side`, `face_sides`, `entities`, `net` and
`attributes`, and the lineage membership as attribution only: lineage weights
nothing. A one-sided row maps `above` or `below` to Palace's postprocessing side.
A Route A sheet with vacuum on both sides is one face integrated from both sides,
which needs Palace's internal-boundary cracking; SCGSim writes
`Model.CrackInternalBoundaryElements` exactly when a configured row has a
`shared_face_group`, so a run that configures no `MA` or `MS` film on a sheet
keeps Palace's default. A sheet over vacuum and dielectric in different places gives
separate `MA` and `MS` rows on different attributes.
:::

### Meshing narrow bands {#surface-epr-band-meshing}

Choose mesh settings that resolve the width of your narrowest band and the
curvature of the gap edges it follows. SGB delivers valid band geometry, but
that does not promise that every coarse recipe meshes it faithfully. A mesh
that passes the quality threshold does not promise it either: minSICN measures
the shape of each tetrahedron, not how closely the triangles follow a curved
band, and neither says whether Surface EPR has converged.

![To scale: the top of a 5 µm rounded corner (blue) with its 0.1 µm band 0
(orange) along the gap edge. A straight mesh edge of length $L$ = 2.8 µm
(red) with both ends on the edge runs $s$ = 0.2 µm inside it, past the band;
the triangle it closes with a node on the band's inner boundary has its centroid
$d$ = 0.17 µm from the edge.](../assets/curved-band-mesh-edge.svg){#fig-curved-band-mesh-edge fig-alt="A curved conductor edge with a thin orange band along it, and a long straight red line between two points on the edge that dips below the band."}

SGB cuts a band along exact arcs, but a linear mesh follows each arc with
straight chords. The triangles stay in the band's group; where the chords are
long, they no longer lie where the band is.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How far a chord leaves a curved band"}
A chord of length $L$ with both ends on an edge of radius $R$ runs
$s = R - \sqrt{R^2 - (L/2)^2} \approx L^2/(8R)$ inside the edge at its
middle. It stays within a band of width $w$ only while $s \le w$, that is
while $L \lesssim \sqrt{8Rw}$: about 2 µm for $R$ = 5 µm and $w$ = 0.1 µm.
A recipe whose elements along that edge are longer gives band triangles that
reach into the next band, as in the figure. This is a property of the linear
mesh, not of the CAD bands: their faces are exact up to the grid, and a finer
size along the edge brings the mesh back inside them.
:::

The test scene `pad_b_bands` shows the cost. It is a pad of about
100 × 60 µm in a ground cutout, built through Route B with 0.2 µm metal, with a
chamfer, a 5 µm rounded corner, an 8 µm hole and a lumped port; its pad top, pad
bottom and substrate–vacuum interface carry margins 0.1, 0.5 and 2 µm, 12 band
groups in all. Meshed through `scgsim.meshing.mesh_sgb` at the default quality
threshold 0.01:

::: {.askr-table-compact .askr-table-numeric}
| Recipe | Tetrahedra | Time, one local run | Quality and conformity | Band triangles' centroids inside their band |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `FeatureRecipe()` (default) | 31,037 | about 5 s | pass | fail in bands 0 and 1 |
| `UniformBoundaryRecipe(near_um=1.0, far_um=20.0)` | 145,350 | about 15 s | pass | pass in all 12 groups |
:::

With the default recipe, for example, a band-0 triangle at the rounded corner
has its centroid 0.18 µm from the gap edge, outside its 0–0.1 µm band. Every
group is still meshed and shared by the tetrahedra on both of its sides.

To use the finer setting:

```python
from scgsim.meshing import UniformBoundaryRecipe

sim.set_mesh(
    recipe=UniformBoundaryRecipe(near_um=1.0, far_um=20.0),
)
```

These are one scene's numbers, not a universal setting or a new default, and
neither row establishes capacitance or EPR convergence. Finer sizes along every
curve cost elements quickly, so choose them for your own layout and confirm that
the Surface EPR rows you report stop changing as the mesh is refined. The [sizing recipes](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-recipes)
list the recipes and their parameters.

### Curved outlines and polygon circles {#surface-epr-curved-outlines}

Keep the number of points on curved outlines moderate. A circle drawn as a
polygon with very many short edges makes the mesh, the simulation and the band
construction all harder: every short edge forces small elements around it, and
every vertex is one more join for the band offsets to resolve. Prefer, in this
order:

1. Draw true arcs where the route carries them.
2. For OrcaPen SC PDK components, pass `curve_sampling="simulation"`, which
   draws each full circle with 16, 24 or 32 segments chosen by its diameter. The
   PDK's [curve-sampling guide](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/develop/docs/usage/curve-sampling.md)
   owns the profiles and how to set your own.
3. Otherwise, sample curves no more finely than the geometry you need.

SGB joins the offsets of neighbouring straight edges at their common point, so
polygon circles build with their expected bands; regular polygons of 64 to 1024
sides with radius 20 µm and margins 0.5 and 1.0 µm gave band areas within
0.02 µm² of the polygon's own erosion. When SGB cannot close or keep a band
boundary, it refuses the layout instead of returning wrong bands, with
`inset family '…': the inset curve at m = … um is not closed near (x, y) um` or
`Imprint lost band boundaries on …`. Coarser curve sampling is then the first
thing to try; the [SGB design pages](../../zh-TW/docs/design/sgb/inset-imprint.html#band-regions-limits)
(Traditional Chinese) describe what each check covers.

## Results and offline analysis

`resolve_palace_result(run_dir, *, expected_handoff_id)` requires a completed
return and the separately retained preparation ID. The resulting
`ResolvedPalaceResult.epr_result()` detaches available final Eigenmode EPR into
`PalaceEprResult`, with `to_payload()` / `from_payload()` and rows/coverage.
`resolve_epr_result(path)` reads that detached JSON without the full run.
`reanalyze_epr(result, *, surface_defaults=None, group_overrides=None)` returns a
new detached result, and `show_epr(result, *, mode=None)` returns a Plotly Figure.
Neither operation opens Palace.

### Native Eigenmode Q availability {#native-eigenmode-q}

The Human-accepted V1 contract permits this narrow behavior: only the native `eig.csv` `Q` column may retain
positive infinity (`+inf`) as its native-reported value during result
resolution. The report labels it explicitly as **native-reported infinite Q**;
a finite Q-based view is unavailable for that value. It does not infer a
physical lossless model, replace infinity with a finite number or zero, or
reject otherwise valid frequency/domain-energy data solely because of this Q
value.

Other native columns and the existing NaN/negative-infinity policies remain
unchanged. This is not a blanket nonfinite allowance, and it does not relax
completion, table structure, mode/index order, request identity or artifact
custody. EPR normalization still uses its actual energy/frequency channels,
not the native Q sentinel. Surface-Q behavior retains its existing separate
contract. V1 acceptance does not establish scientific adequacy or completed
stabilization.

Native port participation is signed and phase-convention dependent. It is not
AEDT's nonnegative inductive/capacitive junction pair. Loss assumptions and
unknowns retain their meaning across detachment and updates; the
[EPR concept](../eigenmode-epr.qmd) owns normalization and loss interpretation.
The [report contract](../report-model.qmd) owns coverage, baseline versus margin
presentation, partial availability and solver-specific quantities.

Shared staged invalidation and per-file persistence are described under
[implementation](../architecture.qmd#palace-preparation-lifecycle). Invalidation
is not a promise of whole-workflow atomic disk replacement. Handoff preparation
never executes or submits Palace; the [execution contract](../execution-profiles.qmd)
owns the selected profile, resources and returned receipt.
